intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an open-air yoga session overlooking the lush Campuhan valley, followed by a peaceful walk along the iconic ridge trail surrounded by tropical greenery. Many local instructors offer donation-based or affordable classes at sunrise.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner surf lesson with a local instructor on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, then relax and watch one of Bali's legendary sunsets. Board rental and a one-hour lesson are typically bundled at an affordable rate.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Attend daily drop-in yoga and meditation classes at Bali's most celebrated wellness center. With a wide variety of styles including Hatha, Vinyasa, and Yin, this is a must for yoga enthusiasts. Drop-in rates allow flexibility across your 13-day stay.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at the pristine, calm waters of Nusa Dua Beach, ideal for swimming and snorkeling. The area is clean, well-maintained, and less crowded than Kuta. Rent a sun lounger, explore the coral, and enjoy fresh coconuts from beachside vendors.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a traditional organic farm in the Ubud highlands, pick fresh ingredients, and learn to cook authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. A deeply cultural and flavorful experience that connects food, land, and tradition.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Take a pre-booked airport shuttle or budget grab taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the ocean and watch the afternoon waves.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate beach strip on foot. Watch the sunset from the beach — Bali sunsets are iconic and completely free. Pick up a cold Bintang beer or fresh coconut from a local warung on the shore.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap Nasi Goreng or Mie Goreng from a local warung near the resort (budget ~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachside warung near the hotel — try Ikan Bakar (grilled fish) with steamed rice (budget ~IDR 50,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash at the airport or use a local ATM. Avoid airport money changers with poor rates. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real. Warm sunny weather expected, pack sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with an early morning beach yoga session on the sand at sunrise. Many budget beach resorts in Bali offer complimentary or low-cost yoga sessions. If not available at the resort, roll out a mat on the beach independently and follow a free YouTube yoga flow. Enjoy the peaceful morning ocean breeze.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (IDR 50,000–80,000/day) and explore the local village and surrounding coastal roads. Visit a nearby temple such as a local Pura (village temple) — most are free or ask for a small donation. Observe Balinese Hindu culture and architecture up close.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the beach for a late afternoon swim. As the sun sets, join locals and other travelers at a beachside spot. Enjoy live acoustic music that many warungs host for free in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit plate and Balinese black rice porridge (Bubur Injin) from a local warung — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — Nasi Campur (mixed rice plate) with tempeh, tofu, and veggies — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Beachfront warung dinner — Grilled corn, satay skewers, and fresh lime juice — IDR 60,000–90,000

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most budget-friendly way to get around Bali. Always wear a helmet and carry your international driving permit. Lightweight clothing recommended — 25°C and sunny.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group yoga class at a local yoga shala or community center near the resort. Many studios offer drop-in classes for IDR 80,000–150,000. Focus on a Hatha or Vinyasa flow to energize for the day. Alternatively, practice on the beach at sunrise for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local beach known for fewer tourists. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling (rent basic gear for IDR 30,000–50,000), and sunbathing. Look for colorful fish near rocky outcrops just off the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the beach promenade at dusk. Browse local craft stalls and souvenir markets — practice your bargaining skills. Pick up handmade bracelets, sarongs, or postcards at low prices.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl from a local café — IDR 35,000–55,000 (banana, papaya, and granola)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local minimart — instant noodles, fruit, crackers — IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Try a local Babi Guling (suckling pig) warung if available in the area, or stick to vegetarian Gado-Gado (peanut sauce salad) — IDR 40,000–70,000

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling to protect the coral. Stay hydrated — warm summer weather can be deceptively draining.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning scooter ride to watch the sunrise from a scenic coastal viewpoint or cliff near your resort area. Bring a light jacket as early mornings can have a slight breeze. Meditate or do breathwork while watching the sun rise over the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local traditional market (Pasar) in the nearest town. Browse fresh tropical fruits, spices, batik fabrics, and local snacks. This is an authentic cultural experience and completely free to browse. Buy fresh fruit to snack on throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a sunset swim. Afterward, visit a budget spa or massage parlor — Bali is famous for affordable Balinese massages (IDR 80,000–150,000 for 60 minutes). A perfect way to rest tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort if breakfast is included, or grab Lontong (rice cake in banana leaf) from a street vendor — IDR 10,000–20,000
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit and snacks bought at the morning market — IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.dinner: Warung dinner — Ayam Penyet (smashed fried chicken) with sambal and rice — IDR 40,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: Bargain respectfully at local markets — start at 50% of the asking price and meet in the middle. Traditional markets are usually busiest and freshest in the early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a longer yoga practice — either at a local studio or on the beach. Try a 90-minute class focusing on flexibility and mindfulness. Many Bali yoga studios also offer meditation and pranayama sessions bundled into the drop-in fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby waterfall or natural attraction accessible by scooter. Bali has many stunning waterfalls within 30–60 minutes of most coastal areas. Entrance fees are typically IDR 10,000–20,000. Swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Kecak Fire Dance performance at a local temple or cultural venue. These traditional Balinese performances are deeply spiritual and visually stunning. Tickets range from IDR 50,000–100,000.

meals.breakfast: Balinese pancake (Dadar Gulung) and black coffee from a street stall — IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.lunch: Warung near the waterfall — simple rice and vegetable dishes — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Post-performance dinner at a local restaurant — Nasi Goreng Seafood — IDR 50,000–80,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong and sash when entering temple grounds — these are often provided at the entrance for a small fee or free. Waterfall trails can be slippery; wear grip sandals or shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) or boogie boarding — rentals are available from beach vendors for IDR 50,000–100,000/hour. This is a fun, active way to enjoy the ocean while working on balance and core strength.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scooter ride to explore a different stretch of coastline. Look for hidden coves, sea caves, or tide pools. Bring a waterproof camera or phone case to capture underwater moments while snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Join a communal bonfire or beach gathering if available near the resort. Many beachside areas in Bali have informal evening social scenes. Enjoy fresh coconuts and conversation with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Avocado toast or banana pancakes at a budget café — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled corn and fruit skewers from a beach vendor — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Seafood BBQ at a beach warung — choose your fish, squid, or prawns by weight — IDR 60,000–100,000

day_by_day.notes: Check surf conditions before paddleboarding. July is generally good for water sports in Bali with warm calm seas. Stay within designated swimming areas.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and reflection day. Start with a gentle morning yoga session on your balcony or the beach. Journal about your trip so far, set intentions for the second week, or simply rest and read a book by the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Hindu temple complex accessible by scooter. Explore the architecture, offerings, and spiritual atmosphere. Many temples are free to enter with a modest dress code. Learn about Balinese Hinduism from a local guide (tip-based, IDR 20,000–50,000).
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Look for a local restaurant with ocean views that offers a set menu or daily special.

meals.breakfast: Full Balinese breakfast — fried rice, egg, tempeh, sambal, and tea — IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Coconut soup (Soto Ayam) and steamed rice from a local warung — IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Set menu dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — IDR 80,000–120,000 including a fresh juice

day_by_day.notes: Rest is part of the travel experience. Use this day to do laundry (local laundry services cost IDR 15,000–25,000/kg) and reorganize your belongings for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn for a sunrise beach meditation session. Sit quietly on the sand, listen to the waves, and practice mindful breathing for 20–30 minutes. Follow with a slow yoga flow as the sun climbs above the horizon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local rice paddies or green terraced landscapes accessible by scooter. Walk along narrow paths between the paddies, observe local farmers at work, and take in the lush Balinese countryside. Most rice paddy walks are free or have a small IDR 10,000–20,000 donation box.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a late swim and sunset viewing. Buy a fresh young coconut from a beach vendor and relax as the sky turns golden and pink.

meals.breakfast: Skip or eat light — fresh papaya and a small black coffee from a street vendor — IDR 10,000–20,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch near the rice paddies — Nasi Campur with local vegetables — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner — Mie Goreng (fried noodles) with egg and vegetables — IDR 40,000–60,000

day_by_day.notes: Rice paddy walks are best in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring insect repellent for the countryside.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a morning yoga and wellness workshop at a local community yoga center. Look for donation-based or low-cost workshops (IDR 50,000–100,000) focusing on Yin Yoga, restorative poses, or yoga philosophy. A great way to deepen your practice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art village or craft cooperative nearby. Watch artisans create silver jewelry, wood carvings, or batik textiles. Many workshops allow visitors to try their hand at a craft for a small fee (IDR 50,000–100,000). Purchase handmade souvenirs directly from the makers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort. Take a long walk along the beach after dark, look at the stars, and wind down with a herbal tea or fresh juice from a nearby warung.

meals.breakfast: Granola, yogurt, and fresh tropical fruit from a local café — IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Street food lunch — Martabak (stuffed pancake) or Bakso (meatball soup) — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Warung dinner — Tempeh Manis (sweet tempeh) with rice and vegetables — IDR 35,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Buying directly from artisan cooperatives ensures your money goes to local craftspeople. Avoid large souvenir shops in tourist areas which mark up prices significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach run or power walk along the shoreline for 30–45 minutes. Follow with a swim and then a yoga cool-down stretch on the sand. A great full-body morning routine to keep energy levels high during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip by scooter to a nearby beach known for its beauty or unique character — look for black sand beaches, secluded coves, or surf beaches. Spend the afternoon swimming, exploring rock formations, and soaking up the sun.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local night market (Pasar Malam) if one operates in the area. Browse food stalls, try local snacks, and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Night markets are a fantastic budget-friendly experience.

meals.breakfast: Roti bakar (toasted bread with butter and jam) and sweet tea from a street stall — IDR 15,000–25,000
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local warung — bring it to the beach — IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Night market dinner — sample 3–4 different dishes from various stalls — IDR 50,000–80,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your scooter with petrol before the day trip. Petrol is sold cheaply in recycled bottles at roadside stalls (Pertamini) across Bali for about IDR 10,000–12,000/liter.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget surf lesson if available in your beach area (IDR 150,000–250,000 for a 2-hour group lesson including board rental). Bali is one of the best places in the world to learn to surf. July offers consistent waves ideal for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recover after the surf lesson. Lie on the beach, read, or nap. Hydrate well and apply after-sun lotion. Alternatively, explore a coastal walking trail near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free community event, beach cleanup, or cultural gathering if one is happening locally. Check with the resort reception for any local events. Otherwise, enjoy a quiet sunset on the beach with a Bintang beer.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast before surfing — banana pancakes with honey and peanut butter — IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Post-surf recovery meal — Nasi Goreng with extra egg and a fresh juice — IDR 45,000–65,000
meals.dinner: Warung dinner — Sate Lilit (Balinese minced fish satay) with rice and sambal — IDR 50,000–75,000

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are best taken in the morning when winds are calmer. Apply waterproof sunscreen generously before entering the water. Rash guards are recommended to prevent sunburn.

day_by_day.morning: Final full yoga morning — dedicate 90 minutes to a comprehensive practice combining everything you have experienced during the trip. Practice on the beach at sunrise for a memorable and meaningful session. Reflect on your journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon — swim, snorkel, and soak up the sun one final time. Collect a small shell or stone as a natural keepsake from your Bali trip. Take photos and videos to capture your final beach memories.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final dinner at a slightly nicer budget restaurant or beachfront warung. Splurge slightly on a special Balinese dish or a fresh seafood platter to mark the end of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Balinese breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — fresh fruit, coconut water, and crackers — IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner — Fresh grilled lobster or whole fish with sides and a Bintang — IDR 120,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing tonight. Keep one outfit and essentials accessible for the departure day. Check your flight details and arrange a taxi or shuttle to the airport in advance through the resort reception.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a final peaceful walk along the shoreline barefoot and breathe in the ocean air. Do a short 20-minute yoga and meditation practice to close your Bali journey mindfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Ensure all belongings are packed. Store luggage at reception if checkout is before your departure time. Use any remaining time to pick up last-minute souvenirs from nearby stalls or enjoy a final coconut on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Reflect on your 13-day Bali adventure — the beaches, the yoga, the culture, and the warmth of the Balinese people.

meals.breakfast: Final Balinese breakfast — Nasi Goreng and fresh fruit juice — IDR 35,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or at the airport — Indomie instant noodles or a simple sandwich — IDR 20,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or meal on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Keep some IDR cash for airport departure tax if applicable and any last-minute purchases. Convert remaining rupiah back to your home currency at the airport. Double-check passport, boarding pass, and all valuables before leaving the resort.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Ngurah Rai International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean and unwind on the resort beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach near the resort. Enjoy the golden hour views and ease into Bali time with a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a light meal at the airport or a warungs (local eatery) near the resort upon arrival — try Nasi Campur (mixed rice plate) for ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — grilled fish with steamed rice and fresh vegetables, mid-range pricing (~$15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and resist over-scheduling. The warm July weather (~25°C) is perfect for a gentle beach walk.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise beach yoga session — either through the resort's yoga program or a nearby studio. A 60–90 minute Hatha or Vinyasa class facing the ocean is a quintessential Bali experience. (~$10–15 for a drop-in class)
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area — rent a surfboard or take a beginner surf lesson on the gentle waves near the resort (~$25–35 including instructor). Cool off with a fresh coconut on the beach afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest beach town's main strip. Browse local shops for sarongs and souvenirs, then settle in for dinner at a casual beachside warung.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and fresh tropical fruit at a beachside café (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled corn, satay skewers, and cold Bintang beer at a beach shack (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Jimbaran-style grilled seafood dinner at a local warung — choose your fresh fish, prawns, or squid grilled with sambal and lime (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons in advance during July as it's peak season. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. Morning yoga is best before 8:00 AM to avoid the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby Hindu temple — Tanah Lot or Pura Uluwatu (depending on resort location) for a cultural morning. Hire a local guide for context and history (~$10–15 for a guided tour). Wear a sarong (provided at the temple entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a relaxing afternoon — set up a sun lounger, swim in the crystal-clear water, and try snorkeling near a reef if accessible from the resort area (~$10 equipment rental).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset — a traditional Balinese performance set against dramatic cliff views (~$10–15 entry).

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort — eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and Bali coffee (~included or $8–12)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café near the temple — Gado-Gado (peanut sauce salad with tofu) and fresh juice (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cliffside restaurant near Uluwatu — grilled barramundi with coconut rice and sambal matah (~$18–25)

day_by_day.notes: Uluwatu Temple is about 30–45 minutes from most southern Bali resorts. Hire a driver for the day (~$40–50) for convenience. Keep belongings secure — monkeys at Uluwatu are notorious for snatching items.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yin yoga or meditation class at a dedicated Bali yoga studio (Jiwa Bikini, The Practice, or similar) — a deeper, more spiritual yoga experience (~$12–18 drop-in). Follow with a healthy brunch at the studio café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a quieter, less-crowded beach — Nyang Nyang, Bias Tugal, or Pandawa Beach (depending on location). Enjoy swimming, beach reading, and peaceful relaxation away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese massage at a reputable spa near the resort — a 60–90 minute full-body massage with coconut oil and frangipani (~$20–35).

meals.breakfast: Açaí bowl, avocado toast, and cold brew at a health café near the yoga studio (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at the quiet beach — pick up fresh wraps, fruit, and drinks from a local market (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant — try Bebek Betutu (slow-roasted duck in banana leaf, a Balinese specialty) (~$15–22)

day_by_day.notes: Pandawa Beach has a small entrance fee (~$1–2). Bring cash as many beach vendors and small restaurants don't accept cards. July is dry season so minimal rain expected.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — the cultural heart of Bali (~1–1.5 hours from southern coast). Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary and walk through its ancient temple grounds (~$5 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's art market and main street — browse handmade crafts, batik textiles, and silver jewelry. Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) for free. Stroll through the famous Campuhan Ridge Walk for stunning green valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance in Ubud — a colorful and captivating cultural show (~$10–15). Explore Ubud's restaurant scene for dinner before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular Ubud spot — Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka for suckling pig (a Ubud institution, ~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Ubud restaurant — try Clear Café or Locavore Nusantara for modern Indonesian cuisine (~$15–25)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Ubud day trip (~$50–60 for the full day, well worth it). Ubud traffic can be slow — leave by 8:00 AM. Bring a light jacket as Ubud is slightly cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — wake up early for a peaceful swim before the beach gets busy. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) along the coastline (~$15–20/hour rental). Great full-body workout with beautiful ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby water temple — Pura Tirta Empul (if doing a half-day trip inland) for a purification ritual experience. Alternatively, explore local beach villages on a rented scooter (~$8–10/day).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar — watch the sky turn pink and orange over the Indian Ocean. A perfect mid-trip wind-down moment.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter, yogurt, and Bali coffee at a beachside café (~$6–9)
meals.lunch: Local warung lunch — Nasi Goreng (fried rice with egg) or Mie Goreng (fried noodles) (~$3–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range beach restaurant — fresh tuna steak with grilled vegetables and coconut rice (~$16–22)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is a fun and affordable way to explore — but only if you're a confident rider. Bali traffic can be unpredictable. Always wear a helmet. An international driving permit is technically required.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning yoga immersion — sign up for a 2-hour workshop (Ashtanga, Restorative, or Pranayama breathwork) at a reputable studio. This is the halfway point of the trip — a great time for a deeper practice (~$20–30 for a workshop).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax by the resort pool or beach. Enjoy a light read, journaling, or simply doing nothing — an essential part of a balanced Bali trip. Optional: book a reflexology foot massage (~$12–15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby night market (Pasar Malam) — browse local food stalls, try street snacks like martabak (stuffed pancake), pisang goreng (fried banana), and fresh juices.

meals.breakfast: Green smoothie, granola, and poached eggs at a health café (~$7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — club sandwich or fresh salad (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Night market dinner — mix and match local dishes from different stalls (~$5–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: The halfway point is a great time to reassess pace. If feeling tired, prioritize rest. The 30mm average rainfall for July is low — but carry a small umbrella just in case of brief afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Tegalalang Rice Terraces near Ubud — one of Bali's most iconic landscapes. Walk through the emerald green UNESCO-listed terraces early morning before crowds arrive (~$2 voluntary donation at entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a traditional Balinese coffee plantation — try Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) and sample various local teas and coffees. Visit a local artisan workshop (wood carving or silver jewelry making) in Celuk or Mas village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner and early night — recharge for the second half of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a warung overlooking the rice terraces — Nasi Campur with fresh vegetables and tempeh (~$6–9)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant — Indonesian curry with roti and fresh salad (~$14–18)

day_by_day.notes: Visit Tegalalang before 8:30 AM to beat the Instagram crowds and harsh midday sun. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the terraces involve some uneven steps and slopes. Hire the same driver from Day 5 if possible for a better rate.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or diving excursion — take a boat trip to a nearby reef or the famous Blue Lagoon / Padang Bai area for vibrant coral and marine life. Half-day snorkeling trip (~$35–50 including boat, equipment, and guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a relaxed afternoon. Try a new water sport — parasailing or banana boat ride for some fun (~$20–30). Alternatively, simply lounge and recover from the morning's activity.
day_by_day.evening: Balinese cooking class in the evening — learn to make satay, tempeh, and black rice pudding with a local chef (~$35–50, includes dinner).

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the boat trip — eggs, toast, and fresh juice at the resort (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat or at a beachside warung after snorkeling — grilled fish and rice (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: The dishes you cook in the cooking class — a memorable and delicious experience!

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling and cooking class in advance during peak July season. The cooking class is a highlight for many travelers and a wonderful way to connect with Balinese food culture. Bring seasickness tablets if prone to motion sickness on boats.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga on the sand at sunrise — either self-practice or join a free/low-cost community yoga session often organized by local studios on the beach. Meditate facing the ocean for 15–20 minutes afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Balinese healer (Balian) for a traditional healing session — a unique cultural and wellness experience rooted in Balinese Hindu tradition. Arrange through the resort or a trusted local guide (~$20–40).
day_by_day.evening: Spa evening — book a longer spa package at a mid-range spa: body scrub with volcanic ash, floral bath, and traditional massage (~$45–65 for 2 hours).

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and herbal tea at a beach café (~$6–8)
meals.lunch: Healthy lunch at a plant-based café — jackfruit curry, tempeh bowl, and fresh coconut water (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a romantic beachfront restaurant — grilled lobster or king prawns with garlic butter and sunset views (~$25–35 for a slight splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The Balian healer experience is deeply personal and culturally significant — approach with respect and openness. Dress modestly and follow the healer's guidance. This experience is a highlight for wellness-focused travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or walk to a scenic viewpoint — Mount Batur sunrise trek if energy allows (requires 3:00 AM departure and guide, ~$60–80 total) OR a gentler morning walk to a local cliff viewpoint near the resort for panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — completely free and unstructured. Swim, read, nap, collect shells, or simply watch the waves. A deliberate rest day before the final stretch.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event or temple ceremony if one is happening nearby — Bali has frequent ceremonies year-round. Ask the resort concierge for current events. Otherwise, enjoy a peaceful dinner.

meals.breakfast: If doing Batur trek: early packed breakfast on the mountain. If not: leisurely resort breakfast (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish tacos and cold drinks at a beach shack (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — Babi Guling (suckling pig) or Rendang beef with steamed rice (~$12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur trek is strenuous but deeply rewarding — the sunrise from the crater rim is unforgettable. Only attempt if physically fit. A local certified guide is mandatory. Alternatively, the gentle cliff walk option suits all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Final full yoga session — choose your favorite style from the trip (Vinyasa, Yin, or Restorative). Reflect on the journey and set intentions for returning home. Many studios offer a 'final class' ritual or closing meditation (~$10–15).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach swim and soaking up the Bali sun. Collect any final souvenirs from the beach market — handmade bracelets, essential oils, or locally made batik fabric. Pack thoughtfully.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience at a well-regarded beachfront restaurant. Celebrate 12 wonderful days in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Favorite café breakfast — revisit a spot you loved earlier in the trip (~$7–10)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh spring rolls, satay, and cold juice (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality beachfront restaurant — multi-course Indonesian tasting menu or fresh seafood BBQ platter (~$30–40 as a final splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing on Day 12 evening to avoid a stressful final morning. Check resort checkout time and arrange airport transfer in advance. Exchange any remaining Rupiah or use at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk or meditation on the beach — a quiet, mindful farewell to Bali. Take photos, breathe in the salt air, and express gratitude for the journey. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and Bali's unpredictable traffic. Browse duty-free for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the calm, balance, and rejuvenation of Bali home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final Bali breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — savor every bite of tropical fruit, local coffee, and eggs one last time (~$7–10)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge — Nasi Goreng one final time (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Bali's airport can be busy during peak July season — arrive early. Keep a change of clothes and essentials in your carry-on. Most importantly: carry the spirit of balance, yoga, and ocean calm back into everyday life.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to acclimatize to the warm Bali air.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Enjoy fresh seafood and Indonesian fusion cuisine as you unwind from your journey.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light bites at the resort upon arrival — tropical fruit platter, fresh coconut water, and club sandwiches served by the pool
meals.dinner: Signature beachfront restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — grilled lobster, seared tuna with sambal matah, and a curated Balinese dessert selection paired with local Arak cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance if possible. Ask the concierge to arrange a welcome spa treatment for Day 2. Keep the evening light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga session led by a private certified instructor on the resort's dedicated yoga pavilion overlooking the ocean. 75-minute Hatha flow followed by pranayama breathwork. Followed by a nourishing smoothie bowl breakfast at the resort's wellness café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 2-hour traditional Balinese massage and body scrub at the resort's luxury spa. Post-treatment, lounge by the infinity pool with curated reading materials and chilled tropical juices.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside dinner under the stars — a bespoke 5-course tasting menu arranged by the resort chef, featuring Balinese spiced duck, fresh catch of the day, and a local jamu-inspired dessert. Soft live gamelan music in the background.

meals.breakfast: Wellness café at the resort — acai bowls, cold-pressed juices, poached eggs on sourdough, and Balinese herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawn skewers, avocado salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachside 5-course dinner curated by the resort's executive chef — pre-book through concierge

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunrise yoga session and spa treatment the evening before through the concierge. The private beach dinner requires at least 24 hours' advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Morning vinyasa flow yoga session at the resort pavilion at 7:00 AM. Afterward, take a private guided snorkeling excursion from the resort's beach — explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical marine life with a certified marine guide and premium equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day trip by luxury car to Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop. Enjoy a guided cultural tour explaining Hindu Balinese traditions. Visit nearby Beraban village for a glimpse of local artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Seminyak — La Lucciola or Merah Putih — offering contemporary Indonesian cuisine with an upscale ambiance. Return to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant — full Indonesian and Western breakfast buffet with made-to-order egg station, fresh tropical fruits, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside warung near Tanah Lot — premium local experience with fresh grilled fish, nasi campur, and coconut desserts
meals.dinner: Merah Putih Restaurant, Seminyak — signature Indonesian sharing plates, artisan cocktails, and dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited in the late afternoon for golden hour light, so adjust timing accordingly. Dress modestly for temple visits — sarongs are provided on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided meditation and yin yoga session on the beach at sunrise (6:30 AM). Follow with a stand-up paddleboarding lesson arranged through the resort's water sports center — perfect calm morning waters for beginners and intermediates alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury day trip to Uluwatu Temple perched dramatically on a 70-meter cliff. Explore the clifftop grounds with a private cultural guide. Enjoy free time to admire the Indian Ocean panoramas and spot the resident monkeys.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the mesmerizing Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset — a UNESCO-recognized Balinese cultural spectacle. Dinner at Single Fin or Sundays Beach Club in Uluwatu — stunning cliff-edge views with premium seafood and cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Light wellness breakfast at the resort's beach café — granola, yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Clifftop café near Uluwatu — light bites, fresh juices, and local snacks
meals.dinner: Sundays Beach Club, Uluwatu — grilled seafood platter, craft cocktails, and dessert with panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Kecak Dance tickets should be booked in advance through the concierge. Carry a sarong and respectful clothing for temple entry. Beware of monkeys near the temple — secure valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Ashtanga yoga class at the resort (7:00 AM). Afterward, enjoy a private surf lesson with a professional instructor on one of Bali's premium beginner-friendly beaches such as Kuta or Seminyak — arranged via the resort's concierge with premium boards and full safety equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seminyak's upscale boutique shopping strip — browse designer beachwear, local artisan jewelry, and high-end Balinese handicrafts at stores like Biasa, Magali Pascal, and Bambu. Return to the resort for a refreshing dip in the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Ku De Ta (Skygarden Bali) or Potato Head Beach Club — Bali's legendary sunset hotspots. Enjoy premium cocktails and canapés as the sun dips below the horizon. Dinner at Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak — award-winning Asian fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with Indonesian specialties including nasi goreng, bubur ayam, and fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: Beachside café in Seminyak — gourmet sandwiches, salads, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak — multi-course Asian fusion tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are best in the morning when waves are gentler. Book Sarong Restaurant for dinner well in advance as it is very popular.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ubud — Bali's cultural heartland. Morning begins with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud. Stroll through the lush jungle pathways and ancient Hindu temples accompanied by a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and the vibrant Ubud Art Market for premium Balinese crafts, paintings, and textiles. Visit a renowned local artist's gallery for an exclusive art appreciation tour. Optional: visit the Tegallalang Rice Terraces for iconic landscape photography.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Locavore, Ubud — one of Asia's Top 50 Restaurants, offering a stunning farm-to-table tasting menu with local Balinese ingredients. Return to the resort by private luxury car.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Mozaic Restaurant or Bridges Ubud — upscale garden dining with Indonesian and European fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Locavore, Ubud — 7-course tasting menu with optional wine or juice pairing (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the beachfront resort — arrange an early departure (8:30 AM) via private driver. Book Locavore dinner at least 2–3 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day. Begin with a 90-minute restorative yoga and sound healing session at the resort's wellness pavilion (7:30 AM). Follow with a luxurious 3-hour spa journey — hot stone massage, volcanic clay body wrap, and Balinese boreh herbal treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy an exclusive private cooking class at the resort or a nearby premium culinary school — learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes including sate lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. Savor your creations for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Lounge by the pool as the sun sets, then enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's main restaurant. Early night to recharge for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast at the resort — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, poached eggs, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during the cooking class — an authentic Balinese feast
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — à la carte selection featuring fresh local seafood, premium steaks, and Balinese vegetarian options

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest day — resist the urge to over-schedule. The spa journey should be booked the day before. The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including market visit if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach meditation (6:00 AM) followed by an energizing vinyasa yoga flow. After breakfast, embark on a private boat charter for a luxury island-hopping day trip to Nusa Penida — Bali's dramatic neighboring island known for stunning cliffs and crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nusa Penida's highlights: Kelingking Beach (T-Rex cliff viewpoint), Angel's Billabong natural infinity pool, and Broken Beach. Snorkel in pristine turquoise waters with a chance to spot manta rays. Private guide and gourmet picnic lunch on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private speedboat. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's beachfront terrace with a glass of fine wine as you reflect on the day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread before the early departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private boat — premium charcuterie, tropical fruits, sushi rolls, and chilled champagne
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront terrace — grilled barramundi, Balinese satay, and coconut panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The private boat charter to Nusa Penida should be arranged 2–3 days in advance through the concierge. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring a light jacket for the boat ride. Snorkeling equipment is provided.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga at 6:30 AM. After breakfast, enjoy a private guided cycling tour through local Balinese villages near the resort area — passing through rice paddies, local temples, and traditional family compounds with a knowledgeable cultural guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bali Botanic Garden or a nearby premium wellness retreat for a guided forest bathing (Shinrin-yoku) experience. Return to the resort for a refreshing swim and relaxation by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dining experience on the beach — a bespoke romantic or social dinner set up by the resort with personalized menu, candlelight, floral arrangements, and a dedicated butler. Optional live acoustic music or traditional Balinese musician.

meals.breakfast: Resort wellness café — overnight oats, tropical fruit bowl, eggs benedict, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Local premium warung during the cycling tour — fresh nasi campur, grilled tempeh, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private bespoke beach dinner arranged by the resort concierge — 4-course menu with champagne, fresh seafood, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The cycling tour is approximately 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes. The private beach dinner must be reserved at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga flow on the beach (6:30 AM). After breakfast, take a private luxury car to visit the Tirta Empul Temple — a sacred Hindu water temple in Tampaksiring where locals perform purification rituals in holy spring water. Participate in a respectful guided purification ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Kintamani Volcano region for breathtaking panoramic views of Mount Batur and Lake Batur. Enjoy a scenic lunch at a premium hilltop restaurant overlooking the volcanic caldera. Return to the resort via the scenic highland route.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy a couple's or solo yoga nidra (yogic sleep) session at the wellness pavilion, followed by dinner at the resort bar and lounge with live jazz or acoustic music.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before the day trip
meals.lunch: Lakeview Restaurant, Kintamani — panoramic volcano views with Balinese buffet and Western options
meals.dinner: Resort lounge and bar — premium tapas, artisan cocktails, and a shared dessert platter with live acoustic music

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul requires modest dress — sarong and sash provided at the entrance. The full-day excursion is approximately 8 hours. Depart by 8:00 AM to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise paddleboarding or kayaking session from the resort beach (6:30 AM) — glide along the calm morning coastline. After breakfast, enjoy a private Balinese Jamu wellness workshop — learn to prepare traditional herbal tonics and understand their healing properties with a local healer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury beach afternoon — reserve a private cabana on the resort's beach, enjoy cold-pressed juice service, read, swim, and simply soak in the Bali sunshine. Optional: book a 60-minute reflexology session by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at one of Bali's finest restaurants — Métis Restaurant in Seminyak, offering French-Mediterranean cuisine in a stunning colonial villa setting. Celebrate the penultimate days of the trip in style.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked pastries, Indonesian specialties, fresh juices, and Balinese single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Private cabana service — gourmet club sandwich, fresh ceviche, tropical fruit skewers, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Métis Restaurant, Seminyak — French-Mediterranean tasting menu with an extensive wine list and decadent dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: The Jamu workshop is a unique cultural experience — request it through the concierge at least 2 days in advance. Book Métis Restaurant for dinner in advance as it fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day sunrise yoga session on the beach — a reflective and mindful practice to honor the journey. After breakfast, embark on a private luxury boat sunset cruise along the Bali coastline — visit hidden sea caves, secluded coves, and pristine beaches accessible only by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat cruise and enjoy a final luxury spa treatment at the resort — choose from a deep tissue massage, Balinese boreh, or a rejuvenating facial. Spend the remaining afternoon hours packing, shopping for premium souvenirs at the resort boutique, and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue — a chef's table experience with a personalized 6-course menu, wine pairing, and a special Balinese dessert presentation. Toast to an unforgettable journey with premium champagne.

meals.breakfast: Resort wellness breakfast — full spread with a special made-to-order station
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch on the private boat — fresh sashimi, tropical fruit, artisan cheeses, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Resort chef's table experience — 6-course personalized farewell dinner with champagne toast and Balinese dessert ceremony

day_by_day.notes: The private boat cruise should be booked 2 days in advance. The chef's table farewell dinner requires advance reservation and menu consultation with the executive chef — arrange through concierge on Day 10 or 11.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning gentle yoga or beach meditation at sunrise — a peaceful close to the Bali wellness journey. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort, savoring every last bite of tropical paradise. Complete packing and check out formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — enjoy a final swim in the resort's infinity pool or a last beachside stroll. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport arranged by the resort concierge. Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium lounge access before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the memories, renewed energy, and deep relaxation of 13 extraordinary days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full premium spread with a special farewell touch from the resort team
meals.lunch: Light bites at the resort before transfer or at the airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout and airport transfer the evening before through the concierge. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for any last-minute purchases. Check luggage allowances for any artisan pieces or spa products purchased during the trip.
